questions.q: What does the --replSet flag do when starting mongod?
options: Encrypts data at rest
Enables sharding on the instance
Names the replica set this instance will belong to, once it's initiated or added
Immediately creates a fully configured, multi-member replica set
questions.explain: Each intended member is started with --replSet naming the set, but at that point it's still running standalone.

options: Adds a new secondary to an already-running replica set
Performs a manual failover
Shards a collection across the cluster
Creates and starts a new replica set configuration, with the calling node becoming primary
questions.explain: rs.initiate() is run once against the intended first member to create and start the replica set.

questions.q: After rs.add() brings in a new member, what state does it start in, and why?
options: It joins as a fully synced secondary instantly, with no sync step
PRIMARY, immediately taking over writes
STARTUP2, while it performs an initial sync copying the existing data set before tailing the oplog
ARBITER, since new members never hold data
questions.explain: A newly added member must copy the existing data set during initial sync before it can begin replaying the oplog like other secondaries.

questions.q: Which command should you run to actually confirm a replica set's health and each member's sync state after configuring it?
options: rs.status()
rs.add()
There's no way to check replica set health
rs.initiate()
questions.explain: rs.status() reports each member's state, health, and replication currency — the real way to verify the set is healthy.

questions.q: Is a one-member replica set (right after rs.initiate() with a single host) a valid state?
options: Yes, and it's already fully fault-tolerant
Yes — it's valid though not fault-tolerant, useful for confirming basic configuration before adding redundancy
No — rs.initiate() always requires at least three members
No — a replica set with one member has no primary
questions.explain: The lesson notes a single-member set becomes primary by default and is a valid starting point, just not redundant until more members are added.
